exercises.instructions: Combine the following sentences using 'such … that'.

questions.question: The boy asked a very foolish question. Everybody laughed at him. Combine using 'such … that'.
options: such a foolish question that everybody laughed at him
so foolish question that everybody laughed at him
such foolish question that everybody laughed at him
questions.answer: such a foolish question that everybody laughed at him
questions.explanation: Use 'such + a + adjective + noun + that'. 'So' is used with adjective/adverb alone, not with noun. 'Such foolish question' is missing the article 'a'.

options: such a hot day that nobody could do any work

questions.explanation: Use 'such + a + adjective + noun + that'. 'So' is for adjective/adverb alone. 'Such hot day' is missing 'a'.

options: such an interesting story that I read it in one sitting

such a interesting story that I read it in one sitting
questions.answer: such an interesting story that I read it in one sitting
questions.explanation: Use 'such + an + adjective + noun + that'. 'Interesting' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'. 'So an' is wrong. 'Such a interesting' uses wrong article.
